verses.text: But a man named Ananias, together with his wife Sapphira, also sold some land.
With his wife's full knowledge, he kept back part of the money for himself. He brought the rest and put it at the apostles' feet.
Then Peter said, "Ananias, why did you let Satan fill your heart? You have lied to the Holy Spirit and kept back some of the money you got for the land.
Did the land not belong to you before you sold it? And after it was sold, was the money not yours to use? Why did you think of doing such a thing? You have not lied to people, but to God."
When Ananias heard this, he fell down and died. And great fear came on everyone who heard what had happened.
Some young men came, wrapped up his body, carried him out, and buried him.
About three hours later his wife came in. She did not know what had happened.
Peter asked her, "Tell me, is this the price you and Ananias got for the land?" She said, "Yes, that was the price."
Peter said to her, "Why did you both agree to test the Spirit of the Lord? Listen! The men who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out too."
At once she fell down at his feet and died. The young men came in, found her dead, carried her out, and buried her beside her husband.
Great fear came on the whole church and on everyone who heard about these things.
The apostles did many signs and wonders among the people. All the believers used to meet together in Solomon's Porch.
No one else dared to join them, but the people thought very highly of them.
More and more men and women believed in the Lord and were added to their number.
People even carried the sick into the streets and laid them on beds and mats, so that at least Peter's shadow might fall on some of them as he passed by.
Crowds also came from the towns around Jerusalem. They brought their sick and those troubled by evil spirits, and all of them were healed.
Then the high priest and all his friends, who belonged to the group of the Sadducees, became very jealous.
They arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail.
But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the jail doors and brought them out. He said,
"Go, stand in the temple courts, and tell the people all about this new life."

So at daybreak they went into the temple courts and began to teach. When the high priest and his friends arrived, they called together the council, all the elders of Israel. Then they sent to the jail for the apostles.
But when the officers got there, they did not find them in the jail. So they went back and reported,
"We found the jail locked up tight, with the guards standing at the doors. But when we opened them, there was no one inside!"
When the captain of the temple guard and the chief priests heard this, they were puzzled and wondered what would come of it.
Then someone came and said, "Look! The men you put in jail are standing in the temple courts teaching the people."
So the captain went with his officers and brought the apostles back. They did not use force, because they were afraid the people would throw stones at them.
They brought the apostles in and made them stand before the council. The high priest questioned them.
He said, "We gave you strict orders not to teach in this name. But you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you want to blame us for this man's death."
Peter and the other apostles answered, "We must obey God rather than people.
The God of our ancestors raised Jesus from the dead. You killed him by hanging him on a cross.
God lifted him up to his own right side as Prince and Saviour, so that Israel could turn away from sin and be forgiven.
We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him."
When the council heard this, they were furious and wanted to kill them.
But a Pharisee named Gamaliel stood up in the council. He was a teacher of the law, respected by all the people. He ordered the apostles to be taken outside for a short time.
Then he said to the council, "Men of Israel, be careful what you plan to do to these men.
Some time ago Theudas appeared, claiming to be someone important, and about four hundred men followed him. He was killed, and all his followers were scattered, and it all came to nothing.
After him, Judas from Galilee appeared in the days of the count of the people. He got people to follow him. He also was killed, and all his followers were scattered.
So in this case I tell you, leave these men alone. Let them go. If their plan or work comes from people, it will fail.
But if it comes from God, you will not be able to stop them. You might even find yourselves fighting against God."
The council agreed with him. They called the apostles in and had them beaten. Then they ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.
The apostles left the council full of joy, because God had counted them worthy to suffer shame for the name of Jesus.
Every day, in the temple courts and from house to house, they never stopped teaching and telling the good news that Jesus is the Christ.
